## Function Basic Auth

Password hashing, verification and the middleware that guards a handler with HTTP Basic authentication.

Behaviour: In package auth: `type Users map[string]string` (user name → a hash string built by HashPassword). `func HashPassword(password, salt string) string` returns "sha256$" + salt + "$" + the lower-case hex of sha256.Sum256([]byte(salt + password)). `func Verify(users Users, user, password string) bool`: false for an unknown user; otherwise splits the stored hash as strings.SplitN(hash, "$", 3), false unless it has 3 parts and the first is "sha256" (a malformed hash), and true exactly when crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare of []byte(HashPassword(password, salt)) and []byte(hash) returns 1 (so a hash in upper-case hex never verifies). `func Require(users Users, realm string, next http.Handler) http.Handler`: reads the credentials with (*http.Request).BasicAuth (scheme case-insensitive, the password is everything after the first colon); when there are none (no header, another scheme, bad base64, no colon) or Verify is false, it answers status 401 with headers WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="<realm>" and Content-Type: application/json and the body exactly {"error":{"code":"unauthorized"}} followed by "\n", and does not call next; otherwise it calls next.ServeHTTP(w, r) unchanged.

Steps:
- produces: http.Handler

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given password "secret", salt "s1"; then password "pa:ss", salt "NaCl"; then both empty; when HashPassword; then "sha256$s1$f9b1214b8df1807692f471b9644de543bee606254884c13ba2e18f598eb2924d"; "sha256$NaCl$6bec8f041f5c92bd702205eb9e39eaae99a019caf941ca18646f37868c220533"; "sha256$$e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855"
2. given users Users{"alice": HashPassword("secret", "s1"), "dora": HashPassword("pa:ss", "NaCl")}; when Verify(users, "alice", "secret"); ("alice", "wrong"); ("bob", "secret"); ("dora", "pa:ss"); ("dora", "secret"); then true; false; false; true; false
3. given users Users{"carol": "md5$s1$f9b1214b8df1807692f471b9644de543bee606254884c13ba2e18f598eb2924d", "erin": "sha256$s1", "fay": "sha256$s1$F9B1214B8DF1807692F471B9644DE543BEE606254884C13BA2E18F598EB2924D"}; when Verify with password "secret" for "carol", "erin", "fay"; then false; false; false
4. given h = Require(users of example 2, "test-realm", next) where next answers 204 and sets header X-Next: yes; a GET /v1/projects with no Authorization header, served on httptest.NewRecorder; when served; then status 401, header WWW-Authenticate exactly Basic realm="test-realm", Content-Type exactly application/json, body exactly {"error":{"code":"unauthorized"}} + "\n", no X-Next header
5. given h = Require(users of example 2, "studio", next of example 4) and in turn Authorization "Bearer YWxpY2U6c2VjcmV0", "Basic !!!", "Basic YWxpY2U=" (alice, no colon), "Basic YWxpY2U6d3Jvbmc=" (alice:wrong), "Basic Ym9iOnNlY3JldA==" (bob:secret); when served; then each 401 with WWW-Authenticate exactly Basic realm="studio" and the unauthorized body; next never called
6. given h = Require(users of example 2, "studio", next of example 4) and in turn Authorization "Basic YWxpY2U6c2VjcmV0" (alice:secret), "basic YWxpY2U6c2VjcmV0" (lower-case scheme), and for dora "Basic ZG9yYTpwYTpzcw==" (dora:pa:ss); when served; then each status 204 with X-Next: yes and no WWW-Authenticate header — next was called

## Function Validate Input

The two shapes of the package and the validation of a client's input into a normalised input and field errors.

Behaviour: Declares, exactly (field order, names and JSON tags as written): `type Input struct { Name string `json:"name"`; Slug string `json:"slug"`; Description string `json:"description"`; Status string `json:"status"` }` and `type Project struct { ID string `json:"id"`; Name string `json:"name"`; Slug string `json:"slug"`; Description string `json:"description"`; Status string `json:"status"`; CreatedAt time.Time `json:"createdAt"`; UpdatedAt time.Time `json:"updatedAt"` }` (one field per line in the file). Exported as `func Validate(in Input) (Input, map[string]string)`. Normalisation first, always (the normalised input is returned whether or not there are errors): Name, Slug and Description trimmed with strings.TrimSpace; Status is NOT trimmed, and an empty Status becomes "draft". Then each field is checked on the normalised value, lengths counted in runes (utf8.RuneCountInString), one message per field, the first rule that fails: name — empty → "required", more than 64 runes → "too long"; slug — empty → "required", more than 40 runes → "too long", not matching ^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$ → "invalid"; description — more than 500 runes → "too long" (empty is valid); status — not exactly one of "draft", "active", "archived" → "invalid". The map holds only the fields that failed, keyed "name", "slug", "description", "status"; a valid input returns a nil map (not an empty one).

Steps:
- produces: map[string]string

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given Input{Name: " Morph Studio ", Slug: " morph-studio ", Description: "\tThe backend\n", Status: ""}; when validated; then Input{Name: "Morph Studio", Slug: "morph-studio", Description: "The backend", Status: "draft"}, errors nil
2. given Input{} (every field empty); when validated; then Input{Status: "draft"}, errors map[string]string{"name": "required", "slug": "required"}
3. given Input{Name: " " + 64 × "é" + " ", Slug: 40 × "a", Description: 500 × "ж", Status: "archived"}; when validated; then Input{Name: 64 × "é", Slug: 40 × "a", Description: 500 × "ж", Status: "archived"}, errors nil — the limits count runes, not bytes, after the trim
4. given Input{Name: 65 × "é", Slug: 41 × "a", Description: 501 × "ж", Status: "Active"}; when validated; then the same Input back (nothing to trim), errors map[string]string{"name": "too long", "slug": "too long", "description": "too long", "status": "invalid"}
5. given Name "x", Status "active", and each Slug in turn: "a1-b2-c3", "0", "Morph", "morph--studio", "-morph", "morph-", "morph_studio", "morph studio", 41 × "A"; when validated; then slug errors: none, none, "invalid", "invalid", "invalid", "invalid", "invalid", "invalid", "too long" (length is checked before the pattern); no other field fails
6. given Input{Name: " ", Slug: "ok", Description: " ", Status: " active "}; when validated; then Input{Name: "", Slug: "ok", Description: "", Status: " active "}, errors map[string]string{"name": "required", "status": "invalid"} — Status is never trimmed

## Function Build Project

A stored Project built from an input, and an existing Project with an input applied.

Behaviour: Exported as `func New(in Input, id string, now time.Time) Project` and `func Apply(p Project, in Input, now time.Time) Project` in package project, using the types of project/validate.go (do not declare them again). New copies Name, Slug, Description and Status from in verbatim (it neither validates nor normalises: the caller validated), sets ID to id and CreatedAt and UpdatedAt to now. Apply returns p with Name, Slug, Description and Status replaced by in's (an empty field replaces too) and UpdatedAt set to now; ID and CreatedAt are kept.

Steps:
- produces: Project

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given in Input{Name: "Alpha", Slug: "alpha", Description: "first", Status: "draft"}, id "p1", now 2026-10-08T09:00:00Z; when New; then Project{ID: "p1", Name: "Alpha", Slug: "alpha", Description: "first", Status: "draft", CreatedAt: 2026-10-08T09:00:00Z, UpdatedAt: 2026-10-08T09:00:00Z}
2. given in Input{Name: "Gamma", Slug: "gamma-2", Description: "", Status: "active"}, id "7f3a", now 2025-01-02T03:04:05Z; when New; then Project{ID: "7f3a", Name: "Gamma", Slug: "gamma-2", Description: "", Status: "active", CreatedAt: 2025-01-02T03:04:05Z, UpdatedAt: 2025-01-02T03:04:05Z}
3. given in Input{Name: " x ", Slug: "BAD", Description: "d", Status: ""}, id "q", now 2026-10-08T09:00:00Z; when New; then Project{ID: "q", Name: " x ", Slug: "BAD", Description: "d", Status: "", CreatedAt and UpdatedAt 2026-10-08T09:00:00Z} — copied verbatim

## Function Memory Store

The store contract (interface and errors) and an in-memory implementation safe for concurrent use.

Behaviour: Declares in package store, exactly: `var ErrNotFound = errors.New("not found")`, `var ErrSlugTaken = errors.New("slug taken")` and `type Store interface { List() ([]project.Project, error); Get(id string) (project.Project, error); Create(p project.Project) error; Update(p project.Project) error; Delete(id string) error }`. Exported `type Mem struct` (unexported fields: a sync.Mutex and the projects by ID) and `func NewMem() *Mem`; *Mem implements Store, every method under the mutex. List returns every project sorted by CreatedAt ascending, then by ID ascending, as a NEW slice (an empty store gives a non-nil empty slice []project.Project{}), error nil. Get(id) returns the project, or project.Project{} and ErrNotFound. Create(p) returns ErrSlugTaken when a stored project has p.Slug, else stores p. Update(p): no stored project with p.ID → ErrNotFound (checked first); another stored project (a different ID) has p.Slug → ErrSlugTaken; else replaces the stored project. Delete(id): unknown → ErrNotFound, else removes it. The errors are returned as the variables themselves, never wrapped. Values are copies: changing a returned Project or the returned slice does not change the store.

Steps:
- produces: Store

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given NewMem(); when List; then []project.Project{} (non-nil, length 0), error nil; and var _ Store = (*Mem)(nil) compiles
2. given Create, in this order, {ID "b", Slug "beta", CreatedAt 2026-10-08T10:00:00Z}, {ID "a", Slug "alpha", CreatedAt 2026-10-08T09:00:00Z}, {ID "c", Slug "gamma", CreatedAt 2026-10-08T10:00:00Z} (each error nil); when List; then IDs in order "a", "b", "c" — CreatedAt first, ID breaks the tie; Get("b") returns the project stored as "b"
3. given the store of example 2; when Create {ID "d", Slug "alpha"}; Get("zz"); Update {ID "zz", Slug "alpha"}; Delete("zz"); then ErrSlugTaken; project.Project{} and ErrNotFound; ErrNotFound (not ErrSlugTaken: the ID is checked first); ErrNotFound; List still "a", "b", "c"
4. given the store of example 2; when Update {ID "b", Slug "beta", Name "B2", CreatedAt 2026-10-08T10:00:00Z}; then Update {ID "b", Slug "alpha", CreatedAt 2026-10-08T10:00:00Z}; then nil (its own slug is not taken) and Get("b").Name is "B2"; then ErrSlugTaken and Get("b").Slug is still "beta"
5. given the store of example 2; when l := List(); l[0].Name = "changed"; g, _ := Get("a"); g.Name = "changed"; then Get("a").Name is still "" (the name it was created with) — List and Get return copies
6. given the store of example 2; when Delete("a"); then Get("a"); then Create {ID "e", Slug "alpha", CreatedAt 2026-10-08T08:00:00Z}; then nil; ErrNotFound; nil (the slug is free again); List IDs "e", "b", "c"

## Function File Store

A Store kept in one JSON file, rewritten whole and atomically after every successful change.

Behaviour: Exported `type File struct` (unexported fields) and `func OpenFile(path string) (*File, error)` in package store; *File implements Store with the same semantics, errors and ordering as *Mem (it may keep a *Mem inside). OpenFile reads path: a missing file is an empty store (OpenFile does not create the file); a file that is not a JSON array of project.Project → (nil, an error whose text begins "store: read "). Every successful Create, Update and Delete writes the whole List() as one JSON array (encoding/json, an empty store as []) to a temporary file in the same directory (os.CreateTemp(filepath.Dir(path), ...)), closes it and os.Rename's it onto path, leaving no other file behind. An operation that fails (ErrNotFound, ErrSlugTaken, or a write error) leaves the file and the in-memory state unchanged and returns the error (a write error is returned as is, never as ErrNotFound or ErrSlugTaken).

Steps:
- calls: Memory Store
- produces: Store

## Function Project Handlers

The five CRUD handlers over the injected store, clock and id source, with JSON in and out.

Behaviour: In package api: `type Handlers struct { Store store.Store; Now func() time.Time; NewID func() string }` and five methods with the signature `func (h Handlers) X(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request)`: List, Create, Get, Update, Delete. The {id} of a path is r.PathValue("id"). Every response with a body sets exactly Content-Type: application/json, then the status, then writes the body with json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(v) (so every body ends with "\n"); an error body is {"error":{"code":"<code>"}}; a validation error body is {"error":{"code":"validation","fields":{...}}} with the fields map of project.Validate (encoding/json writes its keys sorted). Reading an input (Create, Update), in this order: the Content-Type header parsed with mime.ParseMediaType must give "application/json" (parameters like charset allowed) else 415 "unsupported_media_type"; the body is read through http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, 1<<20) by a json.Decoder with DisallowUnknownFields into project.Input, then a second Decode must return io.EOF; a syntax error, an unknown key, trailing data, an empty body or a body over 1 MiB → 400 "bad_json". List: Store.List → 200 {"items":[...]} (an empty list is [], never null). Create: read the input; project.Validate → errors → 422 validation; else p := project.New(normalised input, h.NewID(), h.Now()); Store.Create(p): ErrSlugTaken → 409 "slug_taken"; nil → 201 with header Location: /v1/projects/<id> and the Project as body. Get: Store.Get(id): ErrNotFound → 404 "not_found"; nil → 200 the Project. Update: read the input (415/400 first); Store.Get(id): ErrNotFound → 404; Validate → 422; p := project.Apply(existing, normalised input, h.Now()); Store.Update(p): ErrNotFound → 404, ErrSlugTaken → 409; nil → 200 the Project. Delete: Store.Delete(id): ErrNotFound → 404; nil → 204 with no body and no Content-Type header. Any other error of the store (compared with errors.Is) → 500 "internal".
